text_fidelity_a:
IFAK Trauma First Aid Kit, Micro Rip Away Molle Med Pouch, Fully Stocked Small Tactical Medical Bag with Tourniquet for Military Camping Hiking I picked up 4 of these for Christmas gifts for friends and family. The pouch is a great size, quality is good and holds a lot more than what is included once you take the TQ out and mount it. The shears are a great starter/smaller set, not flimsy like others I have found in other kits. The TQ is your standard CAT clone. I've purchased a lot of different ones from other manufacturers around, and the one provided is the best of the cheaper clones that I have found. With those clones I can get occlusion quickly and easily on both upper arm and thigh placement on large (250lb +) and smaller (95lb) sized people. The windless will hold up well, its is well made and strong. The compressed gauze is a great little addition to this bag as well. The Israeli bandage is well made, vacuum packed and does not need to be opened and "staged" like some that are sewen through. The tactical pen is very heavy and a nice rollerball style refil, the glass break on the back is very sharp and appears to be tool steel or high carbon.
I added about $15 worth of add-ons to make it complete Bleed/IFAK. A pair of chest seals, additional rolled gauze, some 4x4's, some tape and an "ouch pouch" consisting of some band-aids, sting pads, loperamide and Benadryl. Even with the added items, there is still room for more in the kit if needed. I did go through and vacuum seal all of the items I added other than the ouch pouch as I do in all my IFAKs I build for spaace and to keep things clean.

G4Free 8pcs Lightweight Outdoor Camping Hiking Cookware Backpacking Cooking Picnic Bowl Pot Pan Set This is a wonderfully designed, compact set of camping cookware. Everything nests together perfectly—including the two plates, five bowls, bamboo stirrer and collapsible soup scoop, the pots with lids, and even a scrubber sponge!—and fits snugly in the included carrying bag. When I first pulled everything out, I tried the largest lid on the frying pan and it wasn't a tight fit. At first I thought that was a bad thing until I realized this is not a bulky set of kitchen pots and pans; the frying pan is just slightly larger than the largest pot so that the pot will nest into the frying pan to keep it all tidy and compact. The large lid, however, does cover the frying pan well enough to keep it from spattering.

At this price point, you couldn't ask for better materials. The only improvement that would be valuable to me is if the handles were coated with durable silicone instead of the red plastic. The plates are better quality melamine than the bowls, which are a thinner plastic, but they need to be thinner to fit so many into the kit.

We don't go camping much anymore, but what we will use this for is to keep at the ready along with an alcohol stove in case we have to be evacuated and wind up living out of our truck for a while! The kit will also be good to have on those few occasions when we have to cook for more than two people and need the extra pots and pans but don't have any place to store them in our small apartment. text_fidelity_a:
(50+ Cards) Pain Relief Flashcards by Pain-Free Fitness, Exercise Cards Suitable for Stretching & Foam Rolling, Chronic Pain, Fibromyalgia, Physical Therapy, Instructional Card for Beginner, home, gym I have had to go through some learning to walk and hone my body for pain the last year or so due to damage from emf from a local tower. It is difficult to have to go it alone, because I can not have a trainer to help me do this where I am located. Finding these was PERFECT.

HOW THESE COME
These come in a box which lists the color coding, basic info on what the cards are for and making sure you know you are responsible for anything that happens while using them.

CATEGORIES
These are broken down into various categories. There are stabilizing categories to help the body become more stable and then mobility categories to help get freer movement.

DO THEY HELP?
These cards are set up really well. Color coding tells me what to pick from. Once I do, the card tells me what part of the body it will help. On the back it has basic information a physical therapist/trainer would help you with, but it is written out. It tells you how to execute the exercise, then how many reps to do.

There are also comments to help you adjust your exercise for pain or to hone it to help more. It also helps to tell you what is going to be affected by doing this exercise.

I have found that these are basic and individual so that I can do one at a time and work up. If one is not working, then I try another. Or, if one works, I move up and do two. This has been helpful to me so far. I really feel it is the answer to my heart's cry that I could have someone help me get my body back functioning more fully again.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is an answer to a very big problem for me while I try to regain stability and mobility again. The cards are set up very well and are the next best thing for me in having someone help me in person.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am very very thankful for these card.s I have some hope that once I get on the road to recovery again I can regain what I have lost due to the damage done as my body continues to repair itself.
text_fidelity_b: (50+ Cards) Pain Relief Flashcards by Pain-Free Fitness, Exercise Cards Suitable for Stretching & Foam Rolling, Chronic Pain, Fibromyalgia, Physical Therapy, Instructional Card for Beginner, home, gym

Reflective Ankle Bands (4 Bands/2 Pairs) | High Visibility and Safety for Jogging/Cycling/Walking etc | Works as Wristbands, Armband, Leg Straps | Accessories for Sports/Running Gear For runners and cyclists who like to exercise at night or in the early morning hours, reflective safety harnesses are a must. I had not considered reflective ankle and wrist bands before these, and so far I am happy with them.

Like the vests by the same company, these are a bright shade of neon greenish-yellow, a color that is very hard to miss when light hits it. They are painted with a pair of silvery metallic paint stripes which almost look self-lit when they catch and reflect light. These are designed for night visibility and they are excellent for this purpose.

These are attached by way of a 2"x2" square of velcro that is the same bright color. The elastic stretches so that they can be attached without too much trouble even on larger limbs. I was able to attach them to the thick part of my calf but not to the upper part of my thigh - this is unrealistic placement but it gave me a good idea of how much these will stretch to accommodate. With two pairs in the package, if necessary they can all be attached together to make a waist band.

These are well made and should last for a long time. The elastic and velcro are of good quality and seem to be stitched together well. More importantly, the paint stripes do not rip or crack when the elastic is pulled tight which is the one concern I had. Because the paint also stretches, it should not peel which is a very good thing.

These are fine elastic reflective bands that should last for a long time and definitely increase visibility at night. Consider these if you need a reflective solution for nighttime running or cycling.

text_fidelity_a:
Midkawe Punching Bag with Stand for Adults & Kids, Adjustable Height Free Standing Boxing Reflex Bag, Ideal for MMA Reflex Speed Training, Fitness,Punching and Muscle Building Great purchase! Delivered with no damage and all parts accounted for. Assembly instructions were clear and easy to follow. They provided tools that will work but I used own. Easy to assemble, took less than 10 minutes. All the parts fit together easily, and seem very well made.

The base is very heavy when filled with water. It also has suction cups on the bottom that work very well on the smooth concrete surface of my garage. In fact too well. It makes moving it around a challenge, but on the plus side it dies not move at all no matter how hard I punch or kick it. Thinking about removing the suction cups because the base is so heavy when filled with water don't think it will move.

The spring is responsive and can handle some pretty hard hits or kicks without the shaft/bag hitting the floor. It's response time to return upright isn't too bad, just don't expect to rapid speed punch if you're going to really hit hard.

The red bag itself is super dense foam, not a leather covered inflatable bag as I've seen on others. It takes quite a pounding and it feels more natural than hitting a leather covered balloon. I've hit it without gloves no issues, but longer workouts need gloves.

The height is adjustable. I'm about 6ft tall, my son is about 5ft tall, and it easily accommodates our heights. A big plus. It's easy to adjust too, and locks in place very securely and stays locked throughout use.

Overall it is a great product and good value for what you pay. Well made, high quality feel that seems it will take a beating and last. Highly satisfied. Would recommend to a friend or family.

One suggestion: after assembly and initial couple of uses, retighten all the fasteners. Initial use may slightly loosen them. After the retighten they'll stay locked in place. I haven't had any issues with things loosening after the first couple of uses.
text_fidelity_b: Midkawe Punching Bag with Stand for Adults & Kids, Adjustable Height Free Standing Boxing Reflex Bag, Ideal for MMA Reflex Speed Training, Fitness,Punching and Muscle Building

text_fidelity_a: Hornady 46045 Neck Size Die 30 Cal .308 I purchased this neck sizer die specifically for my outdated RCBS neck sizer die with worn expander ball. Hornady's elliptical expander replicates those used by bench rest shooters as it sizes both on the insert and exit of the case from the die. If you have any irregular shaped case mouth,this expander spindle will straighter out the eccentricity while using. I find it a little time consuming if used for other .30 caliber change-overs such as .308 and 300 Win as you have to dismantle the setting in order to accommodate longer or shorter cases. I'm not a fan of Hornady's "Zip Spindle" system as it requires 3 tools to properly tighten the zip knob or the spindle will slip if the nut is not squeezed tight enough against the interrupted threaded nut. A second necessary wrench absolutely is Hornady's New Dimension red die wrench for this propriatory flatted die lock ring also available from Amazon. I lock the flatted die ring and die into my press,then finally tighten the small zip spindle nut using my Hornady wrench. The new dimension lock rings are great as the tightening screw impinges the 7/8-14 die threads at a tangent to the threads thus not marring the steel threads as most setscrews do. I like this die except for the time consuming zip spindle locking system.
text_fidelity_b: Hornady 46045 Neck Size Die 30 Cal .308

-Depending on what activity you are doing, there are some stability problems: If you shift your weight forward to work other muscles, it shifts onto the plastic part and can slide forward pretty quickly; for a wide stance, it can roll and injure wrists; for activities like pushup planks with leg movements, it's really not that stable

vs "perfect pushup"
-It is MUCH more comfortable on the hand. The circular design of the perfect pushup with the rubber grip really bothers my hand to the point I prefer regular pushups, wrist issues notwithstanding. (I have ganglion cysts in my wrists, so to say a regular pushup feels better is a testament to how uncomfortable the "perfect pushup" is.
-It is LESS stable, both in terms of slipping and rolling
-It does not rotate like the "perfect pushup", which only affects things sometimes and to a very small extent. Not a big deal to me.

If this product had a wider, heavier base with a solid all-grip surface, it would have 5 stars, so it loses a point for that.

Wald Steel Handlebar #803 5.25" 27" 1" Black These are a good product for the price. I purchased them to give myself a little more upright position on an old mountain bike. They do this pretty well.

The reason they do not get 5 stars is the top portion where you put your hand was about 3/4 of an inch too short to mount my original twist shifters and still have room for my grips, making the place where you put your hands a little shorter than intended. OK for me, and also wouldn't be an issue for maybe a different type shifter - like the trigger type, or no shifter at all like a single speed bike. However for someone with very large hands it might be a problem.

Beyond that they appear to be pretty decent quality for the price.

Don't underestimate the amount of change in position that you will get. I paired these with a adjustable quill stem, and I think one or the other would be sufficient, so if your changing out an old mountain bike I might start with one or the other, not both. Also, due to the longer reach you will very likely need to change your shifter and brake cables. My originals were cut too short for this handlebar. Its not a difficult job, but a fair bit of work. You probably will want to buy new grips also in case your originals like mine were hard to remove.

My mother recently suffered a stroke that left her a little weak on the left side. I set these up to lowest strength and she's been moving them up daily. I did notice that there are some times when she spends 2 days at the same weight, but then she nudges it up a bit everyday. I think I'm going to "borrow" one from her - she can only do one at a time, but sitting and watching TV is a perfect time to use this.

This is a two pack. There is a dial up weight adjuster. The higher the weight, the great the resistance. The low end is super easy but as you inch up, it gets more difficult. Once it's set, we haven't had any trouble with the weight sliding so when you pick it up tomorrow it's the same as where you left it.

Handles are sturdy and appear to be durable. There are also two squeeze balls included and those work to focus attention on the fingers.

I know she was lucky but with this set, she's well on her way to recovery.

text_fidelity_a:
Peltor Soundtrap/Tactical 6-S Electronic Headset, Neckband Style, NRR 19dB My wife and I have owned this model for about five years with no issues from workmanship. These are good reliable active earmuffs and we like the fact we can hear each other well when speaking but it actively blocks loud sounds. However if you are getting these for shooting primarily at indoor shooting ranges you might want to consider something with more than 18dBa protection. We've found that we end up adding foam ear plugs when there are others in an indoor range shooting high caliber firearms, plus if you wear safety glasses (which you should be doing) it can lesson the ability of the cups to form around your ear.
Lastly the changing of batteries is not great. You basically have to take a small flat screwdriver to pry up the ear cups. Over the years my screw driver has slipped and I've poked holes in the actual ear cup foam! And you need to make 100% sure the cover snaps back in completely after swapping batteries else you will be in for a loud surprise when using those the next time, meaning if not sealed properly it will not block as much sound.
I've found that I've put these aside except when I need to hear someone speaking while wearing protecton. Instead I've gone with a simple foam in ear version similar to this model for shooting: https://www.amazon.com/Hamilton-Buhl-NoiseOff-26dB-Black/dp/B01MYUO3ET
text_fidelity_b: Peltor Soundtrap/Tactical 6-S Electronic Headset, Neckband Style, NRR 19dB

Gamo Swarm Maxxim Air Rifle I cant find my original review so Im making a new one.

Ive purchase Gamo rifles for years so I was excited to see a break-barrel repeater. Well, the concept is good. I have had nothing but issues with this gun after about 8 months. The biggest issues I was having was surrounding the rotary magazine. At first, i was having issues seating the pellets properly in the magazines. They just arent user friendly and are difficult to sit them flush. If they dont sit flush they may not make contact with the hammer. After a while the magazines were no longer advancing correctly and the pellet would not rotate into position. I then purchased several new magazines. They all worked fine the first couple times and then soon after they had the same rotational issue. It seems to be a know problem with no known cure. Gamo created something nice. It would be nice of it worked properly. Avoid the headaches and just get a single-shot break-barrel until Gamo figures it out.
text_fidelity_b: Gamo Swarm Maxxim Air Rifle

I mainly bought so I could see the trailer without the boat when backing, but also use this for loading in wind and/or in deeper water where you can't see the back of the trailer.

This product is strong, reinforced at the corners, metal tubing running up nearly all the way into the PVC, heavy duty PVC and mounting brackets. Those fit a variety of sizes of trailers.

It is not galvanized however, but zinc plated. It will not last in salt water so opt for something different if planning to be in salt or brackish water.

I gave mine a quick waxing before installation (all metal parts) just to add another layer of protection.

Installation was simple. I installed mine under the trailer frame instead of on top. I did have to buy the optional longer bolts based on the instructions, however, the bolts that came with the basic package would have fit. But overall everything was easy, simple and quick to install.

Very professional looking and I would highly recommend, especially over those that only use a small amount of metal going up into the PVC. These can take a good amount of force from your boat.

text_fidelity_a:
Saris Bones 805 2 Bike Trunk Mount Rack After doing a lot of research, I settled on the Saris — I didn't care about cost; I wanted something that would hold my bike secure and not scratch it or my car.

And keeping my bike secure was a huge concern. I have a 15 mile drive to where I bike out in the country — and half of that drive is on the interstate at 70+ mph.

After 6 months of use I only have praise. The Saris does in fact keep my bike secure, it doesn't scratch anything, and it's quite easy to mount to my car -- it takes me about two minutes. And it's very easy to place and secure my bike onto it.

You should be aware that it does mount to every car a bit differently. On my car the side straps mount lower than pictured on the directions because of grooves on my trunk, and I have to pop the trunk to put the lower straps in place.

My only complaint is that the front wheel will move unless you secure it with a bungee cord or velcro strap. Saris sells a separate wheel stabilizer strap; it really should just be included.

One last note: I see people who leave their Saris rack on their car all of the time. It's so easy to remove that there's really nothing to stop someone from stealing it off the back of your car when left unintended. So I always take mine off when I'm done cycling.
text_fidelity_b: Saris Bones 805 2 Bike Trunk Mount Rack

text_fidelity_a: Yukon Charlie's Sherpa Snowshoe My husband and I have been snowshoeing for fifty years, but at 77, we find we can't break trail the way we used to, and the older bindings and the full-size snowshoes are too cumbersome. Over the years we've downsized from the old wooden Bean snowshoes, through the Tubbs 36-inch shoes, and after much research and try-ons, we settled on these Sherpas. We've used them for a year now and are very pleased. They're short enough and light but still track well through half a foot or more of new snow. The crampons grip well on hills or crust, and the bindings are amazingly easy to use. We did find we had to use thin wire or twist-ties to clamp the heel strap back on itself, otherwise the small metal tongue will pop out of the adjustment hole. In cold and and snow, having the heel strap loosen was an issue, but wiring it tight was the solution.

Forgan of St. Andrews 21 Golf Ball Pick Up Tube [Misc.] This is a fairly simple product and, as such, you would think it would be pretty difficult to screw up. The theory behind item's construction is sound, but the construction is lousy. Specifically, I will point you to the cap at the top of the tube; this cap is poorly fitted to the tube and readily falls off w/o much prompting. There are only two things keeping balls inside this tube, the plastic claw at the bottom of the tube and the top cap. If one of these fails, you're left with an open tube that balls can fall out of at their leisure, which is exactly what I experienced. The top cap repeatedly fell off of my tube during use, a couple times from tipping the tube to where the balls pressed against the cap and a couple times after leaving the tube in my car filled with balls. I've owned other ball tubes and have been able to carry them horizontally and man-handle them fairly roughly w/o ever having this issue. The end result of owning this product that was supposed to keep me from having to bend over to pick up golf balls was that I was bending over to pick up balls that had fallen out of the tube. Sweet sweet irony!

I thought I may have just received a defective product and requested a refund from Amazon and was content to leave it at that. However, one of my golfing buddies said he purchased this tube and experienced the same issue, which leads me to believe this product is just generally poorly made.

GymPaws Real Leather Hand Pad Workout Glove Alternative | Hygienic n' Washable | Slightly Padded Palm w 4 Finger Loop SweatProof Back | Mens | Womens I gave up gloves about 10 years ago in favor of pads/grips. It felt odd at first, but after a few weeks, I realized that I could never go back to using gloves. Gloves were bulky, bunched in the wrong places, and made my hands too sweaty and hot. Pads/grips gave me protection without adding bulk, were easy to take on and off when necessary, and held up longer. The only thing I didn't like was that they had a single strap that went across the back of the hand. Even if I laced my fingers through the strap, I could never get a firm enough hold to keep them on for things like medicine ball work. Everything else -- dumbbells, barbells, rowing, push ups -- was fine. So when I lost those grips, I ordered GymPaws because I thought that the individual finger loops would make for a solid grip.

Unfortunately, the GymPaws weren't a good fit for me. On three of the four finger loops, I could see daylight between my fingers and the material -- not a lot but enough that I felt the pads sliding when trying to do some fast work with the medicine ball. So GymPaws were too big for my fingers, yet they were also too small for my palms. I'm a woman, about 5'2", and my hands are proportional to my size, though obviously smaller than many other people's hands. The brand I used before GymPaws provided more coverage on the palm, but the GymPaws left a bit too much skin exposed at the base of my thumb. It didn't prevent me from getting a solid grip on the dumbbells, barbell, or rower, but it was often irritating.

Making a product like this has got to be difficult because you can only make so many sizes and still keep the price affordable. Having one size only is the easiest way, but then it's, 'One size fits all, some better than others.' For something like this, I think the only way to know is to order them and try them out for yourself.

Although I didn't like the product, I've got nothing but praise for their customer service. The return window is only 14 days, but you can return them even if they've been used. That's exactly what I did and I got my refund as soon as they received the package. Given that, I'd say that it's worth giving GymPaws a try. They didn't work for me, but they seem to work for a lot of people. Although I only had them a short time, they felt sturdy and well-made enough to last a while. But try them on every sort of gear you regularly use before the return window shuts, especially if you're transitioning from regular gloves.
text_fidelity_b: GymPaws Real Leather Hand Pad Workout Glove Alternative | Hygienic n' Washable | Slightly Padded Palm w 4 Finger Loop SweatProof Back | Mens | Womens

text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack 50 Lb iSelect Adjustable Dumbbells, Works with Alexa, Sold as Pair These dumbbells are very sturdy and look like serious business!
I got these during prime day, price seem competitive at $300 and the adjustment system was a plus.
One of the problems I have with these is space, since they need to be in their cradle, they take up more space than two separate dumbbells each in their own base. So for a spaced constrained home gym like mine, this is a disadvantage.
Main issue I had and reason why I'm returning is because I couldn't really used them due to a firmware upgrade issue. I received them during the weekend, assembled (minimum required), and tested them and they worked fine, when adjusting the knob, the necessary plates would be selected.
However, a couple of days later as I was ready for my first workout I downloaded the app and proceeded with registration and so on. As part of the process the firmware got updated. After that, the knob doesn't work and I can't adjust weight. If I cycle power I can adjust once or twice and then it becomes non responsive again. So I created a ticket for support, but got a response for a different product. Then I called in, we tried to do a hardware reset and it didn't work. So the agent said that she already had four similar calls, that I should either return or wait for a new base that can take several weeks.
Waiting for that long is not an option for me, so I have to return. I wish the company would give me another option, like replacing with a set of regular adjustable dumbbells instead of these smart ones.
It is concerning, considering this is a company that basically sells smart connected products, that they can have such low quality software upgrades that brick your device and then you have to wait weeks for it to be fixed. I'd think twice before getting more expensive equipment from Nordictrack.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack 50 Lb iSelect Adjustable Dumbbells, Works with Alexa, Sold as Pair

AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking Sometimes where we live, it can get really scary when people drive by quickly and you are trying to go for a walk in the country to just relax. Having this vest handy is really a great item to put on both during the night time or dusk hours, or during hunting season to keep from being shot.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
CLOSURES
This comes with an XL vest that fits around the sides and closes. with strong velcro type closures.

FABRIC
This is a very nice mesh fabric. It allows for airflow and has a slight stretch/give to it so it is comfortable.

SIZING
This fits me and I am between a size 14 and 16 misses. If I were to put this over a winter jacket, I could still close it unless the coat is WAY too puffy.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
POWER BOX
This is ingenious, actually. There is a little packet which recharges. It has a plug on it and also a cord that is USB to recharge it. Once it is charged, then you slip the little box unto a closed pocket which sits under a power button. The box gives a place for the power button to rest on when you press it.

LIGHTS
Once you have it connected, the button is pressed once, and you get the lights on front and back to go on. Once the lights are on, then you can make them flash fast by pressing another time. One more press makes for a slower blink, and a fourth press turns them off.

VEST
The vest itself is brilliant neon yellow. There is plenty of reflective tape all over this vest front and back. There is even a zipper pocket on the front for you to put your phone or other small items in.

BATTERY LIFE?
The battery life of this seems quite good. I have used it a few times and there is still no need for a recharge. I would say you could get a few hours of continuous use at least per charge, maybe more. My outings did not add up to that much yet.

WASHING
I am only going to handwash this without the battery pack and air dry it well before trying to use again. It will dry fast due to the fabric.

HUNTING SEASON
Around my area, fall time into winter can be dangerous. We have had our home shot by hunters by accident, and often there are inexperienced people who try to hunt and they don't pay attention to what is going on, thinking noises are deer. This vest will alert anyone in the early morning or early evening hours that there is a person there.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great vest to have handy. I plan to keep using this especially through hunting season and for late night walks when i hear a car coming.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is an ingenious little invention and I am glad to have it. I am considering purchasing others for the rest of the family.

text_fidelity_a:
Synergee Exercise Fitness Resistance Band Mini Loop Bands That Perform Better When Working Out at Home or The Gym [[VIDEOID:50a12e8589c908f169d5d2cabe52ea8d]] i received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. i was not influenced by anyone in any way.

Strength Bands are an incredible versatile tool for adding resistance to stretching, lifting, and body weight training exercises. There are a lot different workouts you can do with these bands. I have larger and longer ones that I have used for conditioning as well as therapy. They increase your flexibility and strength. These mini bands, each one gives a different level of resistance. I have not tried the mini bands, so I was anxious to try these out. I love the way they feel and have researched some good workouts to do. I wish I had gotten some of these mini bands a long time ago.

YELLOW: the most common color for bands that provide very light resistance, very little tension, which mean that they are stretchy, and take little effort to pull against them and stretch them out. Yellow is used for rehabilitation purposes and to work small, stabilizing muscles, such as the rotator cuff muscles in the shoulder joints. I use this color a lot because of my ripped rotary cuffs. They help to keep my arms conditioned but not in pain.

GREEN: Green resistance bands are medium resistance. These bands are less stretchy and have more tension than yellow bands. Green bands are used for muscle groups that need slightly more tension, such as the biceps or triceps. Good choice for pull up training. Resistance is 50 – 120 pounds.

BLUE: are heavy resistance. Blue bands are for those who are very strong, or for those larger muscle groups, such as the legs, chest and back. Also a good choice for adding increment weight to power lifts. Resistance 60 – 150 pounds.

BLACK: have the most resistance. These are the hardest bands to stretch and pull. Like blue bands, black bands are used for the large muscle groups, such as the legs, or when working with others. Some sets of bands come in all black and the level of resistance is not based on color in these sets. For power lifts. Resistance is 80 to 200 pounds

The wider the band is, the more resistance it offers. You should choose the appropriate tension based on your current fitness level and exercise goals. One person may use a heavy band to do sets of eight-repetition chest presses, another person may only use a medium band. As with any form of resistance, start light and gradually increase the resistance over time.

They do not last forever, they will eventually kind of crumble up and break. But that's over a few years.

These bands are durable, strong and they get the job done. Very happy with these.
text_fidelity_b: Synergee Exercise Fitness Resistance Band Mini Loop Bands That Perform Better When Working Out at Home or The Gym

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Vegetable Variety Pack 4 gallon Kit & Augason Farms Lunch and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply 4-Gallon Pail Where I live it is important to have back up food sources. Sometimes we get severe weather and that can mean an inability to go to the grocery store, no electricity, or sometimes snowed in for a while. I always try to have some different foods on hand that are easy to fix for such times as that, but one thing I have not had is vegetables for long term storage, should we have to go through an extended time of roughing it.

WHAT IS THIS COLLECTION LIKE?
WHAT SIZE BUCKET?
First of all, it comes in a four gallon sized bucket which is square. That means it will fit on the shelf more easily and be easier to stack. This baby was SEALED tight. It has a tab that you pull which starts a plastic strip coming off from around the entire rim of the bucket. The size is 13 1/2 inches high and 10 inches square.

HOW WAS THIS BUCKET TO OPEN?
I have to say that this bucket was VERY difficult to open. If you are older, or have a weak grip, this might be very difficult to open- especially in an emergency. Of course, being hungry might motivate you enough to push through, but honestly, I am pretty strong and this particular bucket was so hard to open I had to get pliers and then pull with all of my might many times to work it off of the bucket.

WHAT IS THE BUCKET LIKE INSIDE?
Inside the rim is a rubberized seal. I would assume that the way this was sealed that it would withstand reasonable water around it- perhaps not for a really long time, but enough to keep the contents dry for a bit should you need to be in the rain or have a flood in your storage area. There is a little crunched up bunch of powder inside which I am thinking was at one time a moisture control tab, but I can not say for sure.

There is a bit more space in the bucket so that you could keep other freeze dried pouches in here, or perhaps plastic dishes or other things you want to put in with it for saving space, such as vacuum sealed spices, or other mixes you might have accumulated or made. It is important that they are sealed, however as you don't want to have bugs get into the bucket over time from just loosely bagged foods. Also I would avoid grains in a bucket like this as they can still hatch bugs which will eat through vacuum sealed bags- ask me how I know..

WHAT IS IN THE BUCKET?
This is where I was a bit disappointed. The outside clearly lists what is in the bucket, but for the price, I expected to have a little better quality than this. There are metallic bags in this bucket most of which are vacuum sealed. Two of them are not, however. One of them is onions, but the other was not even labeled. It turned out to be potatoes, but there was not anything on the bag at all to indicate that it was potatoes. I would have thought that it would be labeled and vacuum sealed for the onions and potatoes. Perhaps there is a reason why they are not.

HOW PRACTICAL IS THIS KIT?
This kit has 109 servings in it. That is a lot, but the problem is that each package of vegetables is the entire contents of the bucket. For instance, it might have 15 servings of peas in one pouch, but let's say you do not want to have peas all of the time. Perhaps you have a quick emergency for a few days and then it is over. The problem is that once you open the bag of peas, the shelf life goes down quickly.

So, once you open a bag, you have to finish it in a reasonable amount of time and keep ti sealed in a jar perhaps for longer storage. It will NOT last 20 years as advertised however once opened.

HOW IS THIS KIT BEST USED?
This kit is best used as a 1 week supply for food. A few weeks at best. That means if you buy this kit, then you will have to plan on using what is inside all at once- at least each vegetable that you open. That means you should buy multiple packs if you want to have a long term storage that you can rely on over an extended period.

DRAWBACKS
I would have liked to see the pouches broken down in thirds or even halves. That way if you open one, you still have another for future use, up to 20 years. I also was not sure why the potatoes and onions were not vacuum sealed and why the potatoes are not labeled. They are a part of the kit, so they should have been labeled like the rest of the bags in the bucket.

QUALITY
The vegetables tasted good- they are freeze dried which means that you can eat them as a crunchy snack food without breaking your teeth as you would with dehydrated food. You can also cook with them, but honestly they were so good as snacks that is how we enjoyed them. It is important that you drink plenty of water when eating freeze dried foods, however. We would always have them right out of the bag at our house which is the best way to have the most nutrients.

I love that this has no added sugar or other ingredients like most "survival" food does. It is just vegetables and that fits our family perfectly as we do not eat sugar or highly processed foods.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although the bucket is very difficult to get into (at least this one was), the food inside is well protected from weather and elements. The food is sealed in large bags of each type, so you need to use up what you open in a reasonable amount of time. Not all of the bags were vacuum sealed and one was not marked, so I give this four stars for that.

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker Well.  I have been using this for many months.  I waited to be provide a fair and honest assessment. This is a review of my personal experience.  My main disappointment is the syncing with the fitbit app - I have a samsung android smart phone with the app installed, further - the app is current with all provided updates. The fitbit 3 itself needs to be "restarted" multiple times a week- you must attach it to the charging cable, push/hold the side button and hold for up to 10 seconds to force restart.  Otherwise it does NOT sync.  SUPER annoying.  And then there are the times when it randomly decides NOT to record my sleep record.  GRRRR....  I have had multiple fitbits - beginning with their gen one version.  Provides reasonably accurate info - BUT if you must FIGHT to get the info through sync - it sort of looses it appeal.  While it says that it does allow you to swim, so water friendly, I do not soak or submerge the fitbit.  I don't remove it as I wash dishes or my hands - so it has been splashed with water.  When I get in the pool, I take it off.  I just don't trust the water friendly part.  I may go back to my fitbit 2 because it is so much more slim and attractive.  These are somewhat clunky.  I also have tried the much larger watch face version - I quickly stopped using it as it is horribly uncomfortable in size alone - the fitbit 3 is much better than that watch face/square version.  The bands on the fitbit 3 are easy to change.  I have not placed a screen/face protection shields on and haven't had too much trouble with scratching - in fact I don't see any - yet.  So I can't say how easy it is to replace the face - or to place the protection screening on.  I wear my fitbit on one wrist during the day and change it to the other wrist at night while sleeping - I use an alcohol wipe to clean the back of the unit and band several times a week. Further I don't wear it one or two nights a week to give my skin a break and to charge it.  I did purchase the perforated (holes in the band) to provide more breathability.  It is a workable step monitor.  I just wish it would sync more reliably and without forcing a restart which you can't just do where ever you are - but must be done while attached to the charging cord.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and I hope this info was helpful to you in some way.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Inspire 2 Health & Fitness Tracker with a Free 1-Year Fitbit Premium Trial, 24/7 Heart Rate, Black/Rose, One Size (S & L Bands Included) I purchased this model/version because my Charge 4 stopped working after only 2 years of use. The Inspire 2 is a smaller display and, depending on the templates you download on the app, can have more details showing on the home screen. There are a few things that I would complain about but are not major issues: first, there are 2 touch-sensitive nodes on the sides that seem to go off when my wrists are bent back and this happens very often which makes me think the notifications have gone off; the second is that I can’t adjust the vibration intensity on the watch so I miss phone calls and messages many times.

This is still a great buy if you only need the basics. All the features for heart rate, steps, and (this one shows) activity time are what you’re looking for when buying a watch like this.

Fitbit Charge 4 vs Inspire 2: What's the difference?
The Inspire 2 has a plastic body so it's a little cheaper in its appearance compared to the Charge 4. It also has a smaller touchscreen display than the Charge and it has a physical button on the side, making for a less streamlined design than the other two models.

Ultimately, it’s lightweight, compact, and doesn’t use up excessive power like other smartwatches on the market. It also charges pretty fast (20-30 minutes for a full charge) and it takes about 4-5 days to run out of power (2 days for smartwatches). I would definitely recommend that someone to buy it for fitness purposes.

Overall, an economical watch that does the job.

Cons: Fitbits stop working after a couple of years for no reason. This is my 4th one in the last 6 years.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire 2 Health & Fitness Tracker with a Free 1-Year Fitbit Premium Trial, 24/7 Heart Rate, Black/Rose, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

The bike could bounce out (overcome gravity) and roll backwards out.

In the garage, you will want a cover over the bike and stand to keep dust and dirt
out of the parts that have grease (the chain for instance).

Indoors you need a long pad (like an exercise pad to keep the dirty tires off the carpet.

Another (better for cleanliness) is a 'work stand' because these hold the bike in the air
and only the stand touches the floor (like a Park brand work stand). But these take about
15 seconds to load and unload the bike instead of 2 seconds like this Bikehand parking rack.
And work stands are much more expensive.
But a work stand hold bike so that you can do mechanical work on it, thus saving paying
hundreds to a bike shop for repacking bearings and such that you can do yourself with
a work stand and some specialized bike tools.

There are lots of other ways to go too, holders that mount to the wall or ceiling,
some have hoist ropes to raise and lower.

This stand is a very sensible and cheap solution, just keep in mind when the
bike is in a garage, then it needs a cover (cloth or plastic). Amazon sells
lots of these covers, they cost less than this stand.
text_fidelity_b: 1-3 BIKEHAND Bike Bicycle Floor Type Parking Rack Stand - for Mountain MTB & Road Bikes Indoor Outdoor Garage Storage

Heat Socks for Women Men with 5000mAh Power Bank, 2 Pairs Rechargeable Electic Heated Socks with 4 Levels Heating Socks, Winter Warm Socks for Outdoor/Sports/Huting/Fishing/Camping TL;DR - these are really really nice heated socks.
I don't live in a cold climate, but I have poor circulation and my feet get cold day, and these are enough on low to take the chill off, and I found medium-low to be great for therapeutic heat.
The socks are knee high and fit a size 12 foot and medium calves with a bit of room to spare. The material is very soft and comfortable and I didn't get any binding, I also noticed less bunching up in the foot area. The heat is indeed all over and feels nicely even. Including a second pair of just socks was really smart. Aside from the inevitable wet foot, being able to charge while wearing makes it more practical to run 2 sets of socks with 1 set of batteries.
I really like the design for the battery packs, having a small button on the battery is a lot less likely to be accidentally pushed than the typical big rubber button on the outside. Battery info is also well displayed and simple - blue is temp and green is battery life.
I especially like that these are charged with standard USB-C so that I don't need to worry about having a special adapter with me. The batteries also seem to support pass through charging, so you can run cords from battery packs to get more use in one outing while also charging up the packs. Starting from full and running half the time on low and half on medium-low, I got about 9hrs before they died.
FYI - most heated socks I've seen on Amazon are rated about 7.4V, whereas these are rated like battery packs (3.7V), so the amperage ratings can seem like more than it is - 5Ah (5000mAh) at 3.7V is 18.5Wh; whereas the average 7.4V battery is around 2.5Ah (2500mAh) which is also 18.5Wh. So despite the much higher mAh rating, these have no more energy than most any other heated sock.
text_fidelity_b: Heat Socks for Women Men with 5000mAh Power Bank, 2 Pairs Rechargeable Electic Heated Socks with 4 Levels Heating Socks, Winter Warm Socks for Outdoor/Sports/Huting/Fishing/Camping

AZLife Lightweight Insulated Self Inflating Sleeping Pad for Camping Backpacking Hiking Traveling (blue grey) I had the opportunity to compare two different self-inflating camping mats by AZLife on the same day. This review will serve as a cross-comparison between them.

This camping mat is twice the thickness when inflated as the [[ASIN:B01HLPSASK AZLife mat that is orange and gray]], takes about one-fourth the time to self-inflate (about 15 minutes), and has sewn-on straps for keeping it rolled up when deflated. All else seems about equal in terms of quality of materials and construction. They are the exact same size when folded into the same type carrying case. They each have an identical repair kit, other than mat-appropriate repair material, and there are identical instructions included with the product which are, thank goodness, in English. Yet, in spite of all that, this mat is priced only, currently, $2 higher than the other, lesser-quality mat. If I had to choose between the two, I would take this mat in an instant over the other one.

On the other hand, if I were not comparing them, I would find the other mat a decent quality one, and certainly, because it holds less air and is flatter, its biggest advantage over this one is that it can be deflated and rolled up much more quickly. Also, some people may prefer the color scheme of mustard-yellow and gray rather than this mat's blue color. Personally, I much prefer blue.

Note that though this type of mat is a piece of cake to inflate, because it inflates itself, the pillow portion must be blown up manually, and deflating it is a lot of work. However, that is typical for this kind of camping mat, so I will not grade it down for that reason.

I have included photos. The first one shows these two mats side by side. The second and third ones show this mat up close.

Note: Measurements of mat when rolled up inside its carrying pouch are 23" long and 8" in diameter. I put a standard soup spoon on top of it in my picture as a means to give some kind of frame of reference for its size.

text_fidelity_a:
Perfect Fitness Bands Pro with Tendon Tech The tendon tech band is a little piece of equipment that so far seems pretty decent for convenient resistance-type workouts. Time will tell how well it holds up.

Pros:

It is compact and light--easy to bring along when traveling

illustrations of workout moves are available on line

So far it seems pretty strong. The resistance level is high--you can certainly feel the tension during and afterward you can feel the effect

It is very easy to change resistance--simply move your hands closer together on the band. The change is pretty immediate (in other words, you don't have to shift your hands very much to feel a difference, meaning you should be able to work your way up over time) and highly noticeable.

The material is easy to maintain a grip on

it feels durable, but as mentioned, only time can really tell

Cons
Not really very many. The biggest complaint I have is that there isn't any guide (even a rough one) as to what the resistance is the equivalent of, as you usually find on resistance bands.

Seems slightly cheap to not include a simple guide to workouts with the band itself (not a big deal though as you'll quickly learn them and wouldn't use a paper anyway)

While the band is easy to grip, it isn't always a comfortable grip. Again, a very minor complaint as usually you just need to work your hands around a bit to get more comfortable

So far, so good
text_fidelity_b: Perfect Fitness Bands Pro with Tendon Tech

text_fidelity_a:
Infinite Discs Slinger Deluxe Bag I recently started playing disc golf again after about 20 years off. Right now I only throw 5 molds and 3 drivers, a mid and a putter. I have the putter in two different plastics, all others I just have one disc of, so I need to carry a total of 6 discs.

I do anticipate cycling the drivers and mids in base plastic, so I foresee me carrying 10-12 discs eventually, but this bag will still handle that. Right now, as a 46-year-old dad, I play with my 4-year-old and 9-year-old boys. This means I carry the 4-year-old's discs and a small jacket for him. I also actually carry a full-size bath towel right now because...boys and water hazards. And there's still plenty of room in this bag.

The putter pocket carries my driving/approach putter and my soft putting putter, the 3 slots inside carry my main three discs that I throw besides the putter, and there's room for all the other discs and kid gear that I carry.

The bag is comfortable to wear, the strap can be moved to the bottom right or bottom left side depending on how you want to carry it. When carried over my right shoulder and across my chest, the bag sits at a slight angle on your back. This is nice because it means you can leave the main compartment slightly unzipped to access your discs and not worry about them falling out as the zipper ends up being at an angle up from the ground. It stands up fine on the ground when it's full of discs and equipment, and it's pretty easy to get the discs in and out of, which was my only concern when I bought it.

As other reviews mention, it won't fit a huge 32 oz Nalgene water bottle, but I kind of plan on carrying something else in the drink compartment anyway. I could get my Klean Canteen in there and I would imagine there are others that fit just fine. The small compartment in the back carries three minis for me and I don't even feel them when it's on my back, but I also feel like my wallet, phone or anything else could be stowed in there without a problem. The carabiner is great and could hold a smaller golf towel when the summer months roll around for me or my car keys depending on what I want to do.

I really like that I can carry all my discs and still have room for a jacket or other supplies in the main compartment.

If you carry a fairly minimalist bag, are considering discing down, want a travel bag or a loaner bag to hand to a beginner friend on introductory rounds, this thing is perfect. I plan on using it for a long time to come.
text_fidelity_b: Infinite Discs Slinger Deluxe Bag

text_fidelity_a: Gootus Bike Wall Mount - Horizontal Bike Wall Rack Hanger for Garage or Home | Heavy Duty Bicycle Wall Mounted Holder for Road, Mountain or Hybrid Bikes Much more compact storage than hanging perpendicular to the wall by a wheel. Bike hangs at about a 15 degree angle off the wall by one of the pedals on the goofy-looking, but very strong hanger bracket. The tires are supported by two L-shaped brackets on the wall. If you are mounting on a standard stud/sheetrock wall, BE SURE TO SCREW THE HANGER BRACKET INTO A WALL STUD. The hanger bracket does the work of supporting the bike and molly bolts or sheetrock anchors will not be strong enough. The manufacturer recommends installing only on a masonry wall, but if you attach to a wall stud, it will be fine. You can use sheetrock anchors for the tire brackets, since they don't really hold the weight of the bike, they more keep the bike aligned and stable. Very easy to get the bike on and off.

text_fidelity_a:
TOUROAM Bicycle Emergency Multi Tool Kit, Bike Tube Frame Bag, Phone Holder, Foot Pump, Repair Kit, First Aid Kit for Cyclist Rider Adventure Travel My kids are all old enough now that we like to go on bike rides. About 3 miles at a time and while it takes us under an hour to do this, it's nice to have my phone with me. I also found I needed to have a first aid kit for when they fall. I've used the first aid kit already, found the bandaid's cheap and wished that they were in a case instead of just a cheap plastic bag. And the white patch kit is also in a cheap case, that whenever it falls out of the larger bag to the ground the lid pops open causing me to find everything shakes the gravel off of it, and put it back. Luckily I've only had to use the first aid kit so far. The phone holds on securely to the bag and I can see it easily while riding my bike. The bag seemed to rub on my knees a little bit right away, but I moved my seat higher and that has helped. The biggest thing though is that even with my small iPhone11 case I still have a hard time getting my phone in and out of the velcro case. I don't want to not use a case as I want to keep it protected. Also, I cannot use my camera while it is in the velcro case because there is no hole. I may cut a hole in it so I can take quick pictures of my kids on the bike trips as I've realized that if I stop, take the phone out of the velcro case and then take the picture it's too late, I've missed the shot. It's pretty tight to get in and out of the velcro case.
But all in all, I love that I can have my phone with me, I can have a first aid kit and an emergency kit for the bikes. There is also room for keys and money if I decided to take my sister up on the taco Tuesday bike trip.
One thing to note is the fit, there is way too much velcro, the straps are super long and if I don't make it as tight as possible then it wiggles. But I've managed to get it tight and think I just need to get committed and cut the extra velcro.
text_fidelity_b: TOUROAM Bicycle Emergency Multi Tool Kit, Bike Tube Frame Bag, Phone Holder, Foot Pump, Repair Kit, First Aid Kit for Cyclist Rider Adventure Travel
